findings.title: Un-timed use_keyspace().await can stall pool refill forever
findings.claim: The `connection.use_keyspace(&keyspace_name).await` call has no timeout, so a node that accepts TCP but never answers USE leaves the future pending inside ready_connections forever, keeping is_filling() true indefinitely and preventing any further refill from being scheduled. Reclassified as pre-existing against base blob ec500386 since the un-timed await and TODO predate this diff.

findings.title: Shard-aware miss drops connection without decrementing total_connections
findings.claim: In handle_ready_connection's shard-aware-port-miss branch, the connection is dropped without being stored anywhere, but inc_total_connections() was already called when it opened, so total_connections leaks upward on every shard-aware-port miss (e.g. behind NAT). Reclassified as pre-existing since the branch is byte-identical to the base.

findings.title: New total_connections regression tests needlessly gated behind metrics feature
findings.claim: Testing reviewer claimed the new total_connections regression tests are unnecessarily gated behind the `metrics` feature.

findings.title: connection_pool.rs already over 1000 lines and grows ~415 more, unsplit
findings.claim: Maintainability reviewer claimed the file is already large and this PR adds ~415 more lines without splitting it.

findings.title: Private ConnectionSetupError enum duplicates ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError
findings.claim: The new private ConnectionSetupError enum overlaps the public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant added by the same PR; a nested match arm could carry both cases and the private enum could be deleted.

findings.title: New test helper unrequested_connection_event duplicates shard_aware_attempt_result
findings.claim: The new test helper has the same body as the pre-existing shard_aware_attempt_result helper except for requested_shard; generalizing the existing helper would remove the duplication.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops single atomic decrements instead of one bulk subtract
findings.claim: The helper issues one relaxed fetch_sub(1) per connection where a single fetch_sub(count) would suffice; only observable effect is a transient intermediate value on a relaxed counter.

findings.title: Undocumented availability behavior change: failed USE now reads node as unreachable instead of degraded
findings.claim: A permanent USE KEYSPACE failure now prevents the pool from filling and publishes MaybePoolConnections::Broken (node reads as unreachable) instead of previously publishing a connection with the wrong keyspace; this user-visible trade-off is not called out anywhere discoverable in the PR.

findings.title: dec_total_connections has no saturation, risking huge underflow on future off-by-one
findings.claim: Metrics::dec_total_connections is a wrapping AtomicU64 fetch_sub with no saturation; this PR adds four new decrement sites, two by a computed count, so a future off-by-one would underflow the gauge to ~1.8e19 instead of clamping at 0.

findings.title: Sharder/shard-aware port go stale while USE keeps failing on refill
findings.claim: Sharder adoption, maybe_reshard, and shard-aware-port discovery now run only after a successful USE, so while USE keeps failing the refiller keeps a stale sharder and stale shard-aware port. Reviewed as deliberate (asserted by a new test) and the reordering's interaction with concurrent resharding was checked with no defect found.

findings.title: New bulk-clear decrement sites' interaction with remove_connection under Arc lifetimes not exhaustively traced
findings.claim: The three new bulk-clear decrement sites were checked against remove_connection's own decrement for double-counting under connection death and no double- or missing-decrement path was found, but the interaction depends on Arc lifetimes in stale shared_conns snapshots that was not exhaustively traced through call sites outside connection_pool.rs.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state test relies on a hand-forged SET_KEYSPACE frame with no compile-time desync signal
findings.claim: The test's hand-forged SET_KEYSPACE result frame was cross-checked against Connection::verify_use_keyspace_result and is currently consistent, but a future change to RESULT frame parsing would silently desync the fixture from the production wire format with no compile-time signal.

findings.title: PR description omits two of the four reviewed commits (total_connections metric-balancing work)
findings.claim: The reviewed range contains four commits; two implement and test total_connections metric balancing on pool clears, but the PR description covers only the other two (keyspace-setup-failure discard), so a reader of the PR description alone will not know the metric-balancing work is there.

findings.title: maybe_reshard's new excess_connections.len() decrement term is never exercised by a test with nonempty excess_connections
findings.claim: The test reshards with an empty excess_connections, so a miscount in the excess half of the new decrement sum would pass undetected.

findings.title: Pool-full excess clear in the run loop has no test
findings.claim: Its decrement is only reachable through the full async worker loop, which no unit test drives.

findings.title: No test covers a keyspace failure on a connection opened through the shard-aware port
findings.claim: No test covers the case where requested_shard is Some with a live connection, where the new arm's unconditional had_error_since_last_refill = true diverges from the deliberate no-flag policy of the shard-aware Connection-error arm.

findings.title: No test exercises a permanently failing USE across multiple refill cycles to confirm backoff increases
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill checks only that the flag is set after a single failure; no test confirms refill_delay_strategy.on_fill_error() actually increases backoff across repeated failures.

findings.title: No end-to-end test drives a metric increment through start_opening_connection/count_in_metrics together with the new decrement sites
findings.claim: The two halves of the total_connections invariant are never exercised end-to-end, mirroring an existing pattern from prior commits rather than being introduced here.

findings.title: No end-to-end refiller test where USE receives no response (the stall/hang path)
findings.claim: Existing tests forge an already-returned keyspace error rather than exercising the scenario where USE never responds, which is the path underlying the stalled-refill finding.
